examples.en: I wore a yellow wig at the party.
My hair was thinning, so I decided to buy a wig.

examples.ko: 배우가 긴 가발을 쓰고 무대에 올랐어요.
examples.en: The actor went on stage wearing a long wig.

examples.ko: 가발은 자주 빗어 줘야 모양이 유지돼요.
examples.en: A wig keeps its shape only if you comb it often.

examples.ko: 할로윈 가발이 너무 커서 웃음이 났어요.
examples.en: The Halloween wig was so big that I laughed.
Natural-looking wigs are quite expensive.

explain: 머리카락처럼 만들어 머리에 쓰는 물건이에요. '가발을 쓰다', '가발을 벗다'로 말해요. 연극, 파티, 의료용 등에 쓰고, 가발을 쓴다는 사실을 말하고 싶지 않은 사람도 있어서 직접 묻는 건 조심해요.

phrases.en: I wear a long wig on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase used with 가발.

phrases.en: When I get home, I take off my wig first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쓰다'의 반대 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the opposite action of 쓰다.

phrases.en: There is a big wig shop downtown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가발을 파는 곳을 말할 때 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a place that sells wigs.

explain_en: Hair-like headwear. You say '가발을 쓰다' to wear it and '가발을 벗다' to take it off. Used for theater, parties and medical reasons. Some people prefer not to say they wear one, so be careful about asking directly.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 구급약을 꼭 챙겨요.
examples.en: I always pack first-aid medicine when I travel.

examples.ko: 집에 구급약이 하나도 없어서 약국에 갔어요.
examples.en: We had no first-aid medicine at home, so I went to the pharmacy.
The first-aid kit is in the living room drawer.
Basic first-aid medicine is available at the campsite.

examples.ko: 유효 기간이 지난 구급약은 버려야 해요.
examples.en: You should throw away first-aid medicine that has expired.

examples.ko: 아이가 다쳐서 구급약으로 응급 처치를 했어요.
examples.en: The child got hurt, so I gave first aid with the medicine from the kit.

explain: 밴드, 소독약, 연고, 소화제처럼 갑자기 아플 때 쓰려고 미리 준비해 두는 약이에요. 집에서는 '비상약'이나 '상비약'이라고도 많이 말해요. '구급약 상자'는 '구급상자'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The first-aid box has bandages and disinfectant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구급약을 모아 두는 상자를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the box where first-aid items are kept.

phrases.en: I put emergency medicine in my travel bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 여행에서 많이 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word with a similar meaning, used a lot for home and travel.

phrases.en: I prepared first-aid medicine before going camping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 아플 때를 위해 미리 챙긴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting it ready in advance in case of sudden illness.

explain_en: These are things like bandages, antiseptic, ointment and digestive medicine kept ready for sudden needs. At home, people also say '비상약' or '상비약'. A 'first-aid box' can be '구급약 상자' or '구급상자'.

examples.en: Since I started exercising, a lot of flab has gone.

examples.ko: 배에 군살이 붙어서 바지가 꽉 껴요.
examples.en: I've got flab on my belly, so my pants are tight.
I envy her lean figure.
I eat a light dinner to lose the flab.
The older you get, the more easily flab builds up.
He has a firm body without an ounce of flab.

explain: 배, 팔뚝, 옆구리처럼 필요 없이 붙은 살을 말해요. 전체 몸무게를 말하는 '살'과 달리 몸의 특정 부분에 붙은 느낌이 강해요. '군살이 붙다/빠지다', '군살이 없다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I stayed home all winter and gained some flab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동을 안 해서 살이 생길 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when you gain flab from not exercising.

phrases.en: I want to lose the flab by next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠지다'는 저절로 빠지는 것이고 '빼다'는 내가 노력해서 빼는 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 빠지다 happens by itself; 빼다 is something you do on purpose.

phrases.en: That model has no excess fat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 날씬하고 탄탄할 때 칭찬으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for a slim, firm body.

explain_en: It refers to unneeded fat on places like the belly, upper arms or sides. Unlike '살', which can be about overall weight, it feels tied to specific body parts. Common uses are '군살이 붙다/빠지다' and '군살이 없다'.

examples.ko: 키가 작아서 까치발을 하고 선반에 손을 뻗었어요.
examples.en: I'm short, so I stood on tiptoe and reached for the shelf.
I walked on tiptoe so the baby wouldn't wake up.

examples.ko: 까치발을 들면 공연이 좀 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If you stand on tiptoe, you can see the performance a little better.
The tiptoe-raise exercise is good for your calves.
Standing on tiptoe was hard, so I came down quickly.
My calves hurt from standing on tiptoe.

explain: 발뒤꿈치를 들고 발끝으로 서는 자세예요. '까치발을 하다', '까치발을 들다', '까치발로 걷다'처럼 써요. 건물에서 선반을 받치는 부품도 '까치발'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 높은 곳의 책을 꺼내려고 까치발을 들었어요.
phrases.en: I stood on tiptoe to take a book from a high place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발뒤꿈치를 위로 올리는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for lifting your heels.

phrases.en: I stood on tiptoe to look out the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 자세로 서 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes standing in that posture.

phrases.en: I tiptoed in quietly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 움직일 때 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together when moving quietly.

explain_en: It is the posture of lifting your heels and standing on your toes. It is used as '까치발을 하다', '까치발을 들다' or '까치발로 걷다'. The bracket that supports a shelf is also called '까치발'.

examples.en: My snaggletooth shows a little when I smile.
I had my crooked tooth corrected when I was young.

examples.ko: 친구는 덧니 때문에 웃는 모습이 귀여워요.
examples.en: My friend's smile is cute because of the snaggletooth.
My younger sibling has one snaggletooth.
They say straightening a crooked tooth takes a long time.
A snaggletooth is harder to brush than it looks.

explain: 가지런한 이 옆에 겹쳐서 난 이를 말해요. '덧니가 나다, 덧니가 있다'처럼 쓰고, 소리는 [던니]예요. 귀엽다고 매력 포인트로 말하는 사람도 있어요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling got a snaggletooth and went to the dentist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 덧니가 새로 자라났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a snaggletooth newly grows in.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 덧니가 있어서 웃을 때 귀여워요.
phrases.en: That actor has a snaggletooth, so he looks cute when he smiles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 특징을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to mention it as a person's feature.

phrases.en: The snaggletooth that shows when you smile is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 덧니를 좋게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A positive way to talk about a snaggletooth.

explain_en: It is a tooth that grows overlapping beside the neat row. It is used as '덧니가 나다' or '덧니가 있다' and sounds like [던니]. Some people see it as a cute, charming point.

examples.en: In winter it's too cold when your bare skin is exposed.
Mosquitoes pick only the bare skin to bite.

examples.ko: 맨살에 바로 닿는 옷은 부드러워야 해요.
examples.en: Clothes that touch your bare skin directly should be soft.
I spread sunscreen evenly on my bare skin.
The bare skin of my arm got red from the sun.

examples.ko: 맨살 위에 바로 입으면 따가운 옷이에요.
examples.en: This is a piece of clothing that itches if you wear it right on your skin.

explain: 옷이나 털에 덮이지 않고 그대로 드러난 살이에요. 그냥 '피부'는 일반적인 말이고, '맨살'은 가려지지 않은 상태를 강조해요. '맨살이 드러나다', '맨살에 닿다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The skirt is short, so bare skin shows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷으로 가려지지 않은 살이 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when skin not covered by clothes is visible.

phrases.en: The cold wind touched my bare skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 없이 피부에 바로 닿는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something touching the skin directly with nothing in between.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I covered my bare skin with a scarf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드러난 살을 옷이나 물건으로 덮을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when covering exposed skin with clothes or an item.

explain_en: It is skin that is not covered by clothes or hair and is simply exposed. '피부' is the general word for skin, while '맨살' stresses that it is uncovered. It is often used as '맨살이 드러나다' or '맨살에 닿다'.

examples.en: After work, I went to the hospital to visit my sick friend.

examples.ko: 회사 동료가 입원해서 다 같이 문병했어요.
examples.en: A coworker was hospitalized, so we all visited him together.
How about we visit him in the hospital together tomorrow?

examples.ko: 병원에서 문병할 때는 조용히 해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to be quiet when you visit someone in the hospital.
I visited my grandmother in the hospital and gave her some fruit.
I went to visit my teacher in the hospital last week.

explain: 아픈 사람을 병원이나 집으로 찾아가 보는 일이라 목적어가 사람이에요. '선생님을 문병하다'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '병문안(을) 가다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm going to visit my grandmother in the hospital this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문병하다'와 같은 뜻으로, 일상 대화에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 문병하다, but more common in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I decided to visit my sick friend tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문병하다'를 '문병을 가다'로 풀어서 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A looser way to say 문병하다 using 가다.

phrases.en: I went to visit my senior in the hospital and came back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다녀온 일을 말할 때 활용해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A conjugated form used to talk about a visit you have already made.
phrases.en_equiv: to visit a patient and come back

explain_en: It is used for going to see a sick person, so the object is a person, as in '선생님을 문병하다'. In daily talk people also often say '병문안(을) 가다'.

en: to be disheveled; to be unkempt

examples.en: I woke up this morning and my hair is a mess.
On humid days my hair gets frizzy, which worries me.
He opened the door with a rumpled, just-woke-up face.
The perm came out and my hair got even messier.
My hair is messy, so I'll wear a hat.
The child's hair was tousled after waking up.

explain: 머리카락이나 털이 정돈되지 않고 일어나 있는 모습에 많이 써요. 자고 일어난 얼굴이나 푸석한 모습에도 쓰지만, 머리와 가장 잘 어울려요. '푸석푸석하다'는 윤기 없이 마른 느낌이 중심이에요.

phrases.en: I went to school with messy hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '부스스한'으로 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it becomes 부스스한.

phrases.en: My hair looks messy because of the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something looks disheveled.

phrases.example: 이 샴푸를 쓰면 머리가 부스스하지 않아요.
phrases.en: My hair doesn't get frizzy when I use this shampoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대로 머리가 정돈되어 있을 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says hair is neat and not messy.

explain_en: It is used mostly for hair or fur that is untidy and sticking up. It can also describe a rumpled, just-woke-up face, but it goes best with hair. '푸석푸석하다' focuses more on a dry, lusterless look.

examples.ko: 풀을 먹여 갓 다린 흰 셔츠 깃이 빳빳해요.
examples.en: The collar of the freshly ironed, starched white shirt is crisp.

examples.ko: 새 지폐는 빳빳해서 잘 구겨지지 않아요.
examples.en: New bills are stiff, so they don't wrinkle easily.
The laundry became stiff as it dried in the sun.
A stiff towel feels scratchy against the skin.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 고개를 빳빳이 들고 걸었어요.
examples.en: He walked with his head held stiffly high.
The paper is stiff, so it works well as a card.

explain: 종이나 천이 힘 있게 펴져 있어서 잘 구부러지지 않는 느낌이에요. 반대는 '구겨지다, 흐물흐물하다' 쪽이고, 몸이 굳은 건 보통 '뻣뻣하다'라고 해요. '고개를 빳빳이 들다'는 당당하거나 거만한 태도를 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I made a card out of stiff paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘 있게 펴져서 잘 구부러지지 않는 물건 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun that holds its shape and does not bend easily.

phrases.en: I ironed my shirt crisp and put it on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 다려서 주름 없이 힘 있게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ironing clothes until they are crisp and wrinkle-free.

phrases.example: 그는 잘못하고도 고개를 빳빳이 들고 있어요.
phrases.en: He holds his head up stiffly even though he did wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당당하거나 거만한 태도를 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for a proud or arrogant attitude.

explain_en: It gives the feel of paper or cloth that is firm and straight and doesn't bend easily. Its opposite is closer to '구겨지다' (wrinkled) or '흐물흐물하다' (floppy), and a stiff body is usually '뻣뻣하다'. '고개를 빳빳이 들다' can also describe a proud or arrogant attitude.

examples.ko: 저는 눈이 나빠서 뿔테 안경을 써요.
examples.en: My eyesight is bad, so I wear thick-framed glasses.
With thick-rimmed glasses on, your impression looks different.
I switched my glasses from gold frames to thick frames.
They say black thick frames suit your face.

examples.ko: 뿔테는 가볍고 튼튼한 걸로 골라 주세요.
examples.en: Please pick thick frames that are light and sturdy.

examples.ko: 친구는 뿔테에 렌즈를 바꾸러 안경점에 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend went to the optician to change the lenses in the thick frames.

explain: 원래 뿔로 만든 안경테를 말했지만, 요즘은 두껍고 둥근 플라스틱 테 안경도 보통 '뿔테'라고 해요. 금속 테는 '금테, 은테'처럼 부르고, 테가 없는 건 '무테'라고 해요.

phrases.en: You look intellectual when you wear horn-rimmed glasses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔히 쓰는 짝말로, 두꺼운 테의 안경을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning glasses with thick frames.

phrases.en: I like light rimless glasses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 테가 아예 없는 안경으로, 뿔테와 반대되는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Glasses with no frame at all, the opposite of 뿔테.

phrases.en: My grandfather wears gold-rimmed glasses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금속 테 안경 중 금색 테를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gold-colored metal frame, as opposed to plastic.

explain_en: It originally meant frames made of horn, but today thick plastic frames are also commonly called '뿔테'. Metal frames are called things like '금테' (gold) and '은테' (silver), and frameless ones are '무테'.

examples.en: I always wash my face before bed in the evening.
Washing your face with lukewarm water is good for your skin.
After removing makeup, I washed my face slowly.

examples.ko: 아침에 세안하는 데 오 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about five minutes to wash my face in the morning.
Even when tired, you must wash your face for clean skin.
I was too sleepy yesterday and couldn't wash my face.

explain: '세수하다'가 훨씬 자연스러운 일상어예요. 화장을 지우고 닦는 것까지 말할 때는 '세안하다'를 쓰고, 얼굴에만 써요. 몸 전체는 '샤워하다', '씻다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I wash my face right after getting up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 일상에서 더 자연스러워요. 화장품 이야기에서는 '세안하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning but more natural in daily life. '세안하다' fits skincare contexts.

phrases.en: I put on lotion after washing my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다음에 할 일을 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to say what comes after washing the face.

phrases.en: I was tired, so I went to sleep without washing my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않고'는 하지 않은 채 다른 일을 했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-지 않고' means doing something else without doing the first thing.
phrases.en_equiv: to sleep without washing the face

explain_en: 세수하다 is the far more natural everyday word. 세안하다 is used when talking about cleansing off makeup, and only for the face. For the whole body, use 샤워하다 or 씻다.

examples.en: When you're nervous, try taking slow deep breaths.
I took a big deep breath before the presentation.
After exercising, I rested while breathing deeply.
Just taking a deep breath calms the mind.
The teacher told everyone to take a deep breath.
I took a deep breath before entering the exam room and went in.

explain: '숨을 쉬다'가 기본 호흡이라면 '심호흡하다'는 일부러 숨을 깊게 들이쉬고 내쉬는 것이에요. 긴장을 풀거나 마음을 가라앉힐 때 쓰는 말이에요. '숨을 깊이 쉬다'보다 짧고 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 긴장될 때 심호흡을 한 번 해요.
phrases.en: When I feel nervous, I take one deep breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심호흡하다'와 뜻이 같고, '을/를'을 넣어 말할 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 심호흡하다, with the object particle added.

phrases.example: 화가 나면 숨을 깊이 쉬어 보세요.
phrases.en: When you get angry, try breathing deeply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 풀어서 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more spelled-out way of saying it.

phrases.en: After taking a deep breath, I opened the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심호흡한 다음에 다른 행동을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when another action follows the deep breath.

explain_en: 숨을 쉬다 is ordinary breathing, while 심호흡하다 is deliberately breathing in and out deeply. It is used to relax or calm down. It is shorter and more natural than 숨을 깊이 쉬다.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 신랑이 신부의 약지에 반지를 끼워 줬어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, the groom put the ring on the bride's ring finger.
I broke my right ring finger and got a cast.

examples.ko: 기타를 칠 때 약지는 힘이 잘 안 들어가요.
examples.en: When I play guitar, my ring finger doesn't get much strength.

examples.ko: 약지를 다쳐서 반지를 뺄 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I hurt my ring finger, so I can't take the ring off.

examples.ko: 왼손 약지 사이즈를 재서 반지를 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I had my left ring finger measured and ordered a ring.
Try folding your ring finger and pinky together.

explain: '약손가락'과 같은 말이에요. 한자어라서 병원, 설명문, 뉴스에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '약손가락'이 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.

phrases.en: I put a ring on my ring finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning and sounds softer in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I wear a ring on my left ring finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 손인지 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying which hand it is.

phrases.en: I hurt my ring finger while exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 아픈 곳을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used to tell a doctor where it hurts.

explain_en: It means the same as '약손가락'. As a Sino-Korean word, it appears at hospitals, in explanations and in the news, while '약손가락' sounds a bit softer in everyday conversation.

examples.en: I dressed up neatly in a hanbok and took photos.

examples.ko: 내일 면접이라서 정장을 말끔하게 차려입을 거예요.
examples.en: I have an interview tomorrow, so I'll dress up in a neat suit.
Why are you dressed up so nicely today?

examples.ko: 결혼식에 갈 때는 단정하게 차려입는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When going to a wedding, it's good to dress neatly.
I usually dress casually, but I dress up for gatherings.
You look really great all dressed up.

explain: 그냥 '입다'와 달리 격식에 맞게 신경 써서 단정히 입는다는 느낌이에요. '옷을 차려입다'로 쓰고, 멋을 내는 느낌이면 '빼입다'라는 말도 있어요. 평소 옷에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: I dressed up nicely and went to the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 격식 있게 입고 어디에 갔다고 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for saying you dressed up and then went somewhere.

phrases.en: You look great dressed up in a suit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단정하게 입은 모습을 설명하거나 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe or compliment someone's neat, dressed-up appearance.

phrases.en: My friend came dressed to impress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 격식보다 멋을 내서 입었다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, with more of a feeling of dressing stylishly than formally.

explain_en: Unlike plain '입다', it suggests putting on clothes carefully and properly for the occasion. It is used as '옷을 차려입다', and there is also '빼입다' for dressing up stylishly. It doesn't fit everyday casual clothes.

en: brim; bill; visor (of a cap or hat)

examples.en: The brim of the hat blocks the sunlight.
I bought a wide-brimmed hat.
The hat brim got bent by the wind.
He pulled the visor down over his eyes.
I wrote my name on the brim of my baseball cap.

examples.ko: 챙 없는 모자는 햇볕에 얼굴이 타요.
examples.en: With a hat that has no brim, your face gets sunburned.

explain: '챙'은 모자 앞이나 둘레에 튀어나온 부분이에요. 야구 모자는 앞쪽에만 있고, 밀짚모자는 둘레에 둥글게 있어요. 소리가 비슷한 '챙기다'는 준비해서 가져간다는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 햇빛이 강해서 챙이 긴 모자를 썼어요.
phrases.en: The sun was strong, so I wore a hat with a long brim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 챙의 길이로 모자의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a hat by the length of its brim.

phrases.en: The light was bright, so I pulled down my hat brim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇빛을 가리려고 챙을 아래로 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when lowering the brim to block sunlight.
phrases.en_equiv: to pull down the hat brim

phrases.en: I like hats without a brim.
phrases.nuance_ko: '없는'을 붙여서 챙이 없는 모자를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '없는' describes a hat that has no brim.

explain_en: 챙 is the part of a hat that sticks out at the front or all the way around. A baseball cap has it only at the front, while a straw hat has a round one. The similar-sounding 챙기다 is a different word meaning to get something ready and take it along.

examples.en: My nose hair was sticking out, so I cut it with scissors.
When you pull out nose hair, your eyes water.
I received a nose hair trimmer as a gift.

examples.ko: 먼지를 걸러 주는 코털도 하는 일이 있어요.
examples.en: Nose hair has a job too, filtering out dust.
Before the interview, I even neatly trimmed my nose hair.
My husband is worried about his nose hair.

explain: '코털을 뽑다/자르다/다듬다'처럼 써요. 일상에서 흔한 말이지만 조금 민망한 주제라서 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 꺼내지 않아요. 편한 사이에서 외모 이야기를 할 때 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: I pulled out a nose hair and my eyes watered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손이나 도구로 뽑는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to pulling nose hair out by hand or with a tool.

phrases.en: Trimming nose hair with scissors looks neat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가위나 기계로 자를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cutting with scissors or a trimmer.

phrases.en: I trim my nose hair before going out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧고 단정하게 정리한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the feel of tidying up neatly.

explain_en: It goes with verbs such as '코털을 뽑다/자르다/다듬다'. It is a common word, but the topic is a little embarrassing, so people avoid it in formal settings. It mostly comes up between close people talking about appearance.

examples.en: In spring I often wear a thin trench coat.
It was raining, so I went out wearing a trench coat.
This trench coat has a belt at the waist.
For trench coats, beige is the most popular color.
I bought a trench coat to wear in autumn.
If you wear a knit under a trench coat, you stay warm.

explain: 허리에 벨트가 있고 길이가 긴 얇은 겉옷이에요. 한국에서는 봄과 가을에 많이 입어서 '환절기 코트'라는 느낌이 있어요. 겨울 코트처럼 두껍지 않아서 '코트'와 따로 이야기하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 베이지색 트렌치코트를 입고 있었어요.
phrases.en: That person was wearing a beige trench coat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 트렌치코트는 베이지색이 가장 흔해서 이렇게 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Beige is the most common color for trench coats, so people often say it this way.

phrases.example: 가을에 입으려고 트렌치코트 한 벌을 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought a trench coat to wear in the fall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 셀 때는 '벌'을 써요. 가게에서 살 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counter for clothes is '벌'. Often said when shopping.

phrases.en: It was chilly, so I threw on a trench coat and went out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입다'보다 가볍게 겉에 두른다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels lighter than '입다', like casually putting something on over your clothes.
phrases.en_equiv: to throw on a trench coat

explain_en: It's a thin, long outer coat with a belt at the waist. In Korea it's worn a lot in spring and autumn, so it has the feel of a 'between-seasons coat'. Since it isn't thick like a winter coat, people often talk about it separately from a regular '코트'.

en: pillowing one's head on someone's arm; pillow of one's arm

examples.ko: 그는 팔베개를 하고 누워서 천장을 봤어요.
examples.en: He lay with his arm under his head and looked at the ceiling.
The child fell asleep with Dad's arm as a pillow.
If you give someone an arm pillow, your arm goes numb.
I lay on the grass with my arm as a pillow and watched the clouds.

examples.ko: 남편이 팔베개를 해 줘서 금방 잠이 왔어요.
examples.en: My husband gave me his arm as a pillow, so I fell asleep quickly.
We talked for a long time lying with an arm pillow.

explain: '팔베개를 하다'는 자기 팔을 베는 것도, 남에게 자기 팔을 베게 해 주는 것도 돼요. 이때는 '해 주다'를 붙여서 구분해요. 편하게 눕거나 가까운 사이에서 하는 모습을 말해요.

phrases.en: The mother let the child use her arm as a pillow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 내 팔을 베게 해 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means letting someone rest their head on your arm.
phrases.en_equiv: to give someone an arm pillow

phrases.example: 저는 팔베개를 하고 누워서 음악을 들었어요.
phrases.en: I lay with my head on my arm and listened to music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 팔을 베고 눕는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes lying with your head on your own arm.
phrases.en_equiv: to use one's arm as a pillow

phrases.example: 아이는 아빠 팔베개하고 자는 걸 좋아해요.
phrases.en: The child likes sleeping on dad's arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자면서 팔을 베는 모습이에요. 가까운 사이에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sleeping while resting on an arm. Used mostly between people who are close.

explain_en: '팔베개를 하다' can mean using your own arm as a pillow, or letting someone else rest on your arm; add '해 주다' for the latter. It describes a relaxed lying posture, or something done between close people.
